evidence: validate_proof_artifact checked each execution's state but never compared its subject_scope_digest with the artifact's, so the field was decorative and any syntactically valid digest passed. A passing record copied from an older or unrelated subject certified the current proof.

concrete independently established defect
resolution_evidence: An execution must now carry the artifact's own subject scope digest. findings.summary: The round-8 anti-ratchet fix made the plan's own inactive -> migration baseline transition unreachable.
evidence: The A2-R8-001 remediation rejected every addition measured against a trusted prior. Section 3.9 declares inactive -> migration legal and an inactive baseline is required to be mechanically empty, so entering migration necessarily adds items and was left unreachable. Reproduced against the repository's own committed temporary-activation-baseline.json, which is inactive and empty: inactive -> migration([V-001]) raised ActivationBaselineError at c927a95 and was accepted at a034fc3, so the regression was introduced by the round-8 fix itself. No fixture caught it because every prior_baseline test in the suite passed a migration prior -- round 8's own lesson about fixture-bounded differentials, recurring in the commit that recorded it.
requirement_property: integration-plan 3.9 (the baseline modes are inactive -> migration -> strict)
common.schema.json baseline_mode_transitions (inactive -> migration is declared legal)
concrete independently established defect, reproduced against the committed baseline
resolution_evidence: Additions are now permitted only on the inactive -> migration edge, the single act 3.9 requires to exist: cataloguing the pre-existing set. The exemption cannot be re-entered because no transition returns to inactive, so the catalogue is populated exactly once and never grows again; growth from a migration prior stays rejected and is locked. Three fixtures are added, two of which fail at c927a95, and one asserts the committed baseline document rather than a constructed one.

findings.summary: REFERENCE_SEMANTICS_VERSION stayed at 2.0.0 across three changes to what the executable semantics accept or reject.
evidence: Rounds 8 and 9 changed three admission rules -- activation-baseline admission, proof execution/subject binding, and disable-anchor validation -- while REFERENCE_SEMANTICS_VERSION stayed at 2.0.0. That value is a field of the proof-closure subject, so it is an INPUT to subject_scope_digest, and assess_proof_freshness compares it by equality to raise proof-semantics-changed. Two materially different semantic policies sharing one value defeats that identity contract. The module's own history sets the rule it departed from: 1.0.0 -> 1.9.0 bumped once per semantic-change commit, and plan v0.19 reserved MAJOR for the import-contract break. test_reference_semantics_version_is_pinned existed throughout and did not help: it asserts the value is what it is, never that it moved when the semantics did, so both rounds passed green with the line untouched.
requirement_property: integration-plan v0.19 (the semantics version is stamped into every proof snapshot)
assess_proof_freshness proof-semantics-changed equality comparison
concrete independently established defect
resolution_evidence: Advanced to 2.1.0 -- MINOR, per the module's own precedent -- covering the round-8 and round-9 changes together, restored rather than back-dated. The policy is now stated at the constant itself, since leaving it implicit is what let it lapse. No proof artifact exists in the repository, so nothing recorded is invalidated: the bump is mechanically inert today and is made for honest signalling, the same reasoning plan v0.19 applied when it restored 2.0.0. A fixture now locks the constant to every document that cites it; whether a bump was OWED remains a judgement no mechanism can settle, and that limit is recorded in the pin's own docstring rather than implied away.
